citations.assessment: The Bavli gives both alternatives. The checked edition also changes Aḥa to Aḥi in the second formulation, while Heilprin reports a single spelling.
The dialogue names Tanhum as accustomed to studying with R. Yehoshua ben Levi. Tanhum expressly distinguishes his report from one heard from that teacher.
Midrash Tehillim §139 has a separate teaching from Shmuel bar Tanḥum under the Psalm’s opening, rather than the tablets dialogue. The closest implications concern name form only.
Shir HaShirim Rabbah identifies Shmuel bar Tanḥum and Ḥanan son of R. Berekhiah Botzerya as reporting Yirmeyah. It is the peace exposition rather than Tanhum’s tablets dialogue.
The Yalkut gives Shmuel bar R. Tanḥuma, Ḥanin bar R. and Berekhiah ben Tzeruyah citing Idi. The names are printed separately.
The parallel names Shmuel bar Tanḥum and R. Ḥana citing Idi, where Heilprin gives Ḥanin.

notes.text: Bava Kamma 55a:2 gives the alternatives uncle of Rav Aḥa and grandfather of Rav Aḥi. Heilprin uses Aḥa in both.
The Midrash Hazit, Yalkut and Bereshit Rabbah parallels discuss Israel bringing peace to the world. They have related but different names from the Bava Kamma dialogue about the tablets.
